items.followUp: State the head-to-tail rule for adding three vectors.

rubric.why: The rule requires consecutive placement of the vectors.
rubric.description: Places each vector’s tail at the previous vector’s head.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining the consecutive head-to-tail arrangement.

rubric.why: The resultant is drawn from the start of the first vector to the end of the last.
rubric.description: Identifies the direction and endpoints of the resultant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating how to draw the resultant.

modelAnswer: Place the tail of each vector at the head of the preceding vector, head to tail.
The resultant is drawn from the tail of the first vector to the head of the last vector.

items.followUp: Define the resolution of a force and state what its components represent.

rubric.why: Resolution means replacing a force by components.
rubric.description: Defines resolution as splitting a force into components.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a force is split or resolved into components.

rubric.why: The components act in specified directions and together represent the original force.
rubric.description: States the directions or equivalent effect of the components.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning specified directions or that the components together have the effect of the original force.

modelAnswer: The process of splitting a force into components along specified directions is called resolution of a force.
These components together have the same effect as the original force.

items.followUp: What is a contact force? Give one example.

rubric.why: A field force acts without the objects touching.
rubric.description: States that a field force acts without physical contact.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its non-contact action.

rubric.why: Field forces act through a field; examples include gravitational, magnetic, and electrostatic forces.
rubric.description: Identifies action through a field or gives a valid example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it acts through a field or giving a valid field-force example.

modelAnswer: A field force is a force that acts between objects without physical contact.
It acts through a field, for example, gravitational, magnetic or electrostatic force.

items.followUp: Define work and write its SI unit.

rubric.why: Power measures how quickly work is done or energy is transferred.
rubric.description: Defines power as the rate of doing work or transferring energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the rate-based definition.

rubric.why: The SI unit of power is the watt.
rubric.description: Gives the SI unit of power.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for writing watt or W.

modelAnswer: Power is the rate of doing work.
Its SI unit is the watt (W).

items.followUp: Define kinetic energy and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: Energy is described as the capacity or ability to do work.
rubric.description: Defines energy as the capacity to do work.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

rubric.why: The SI unit of energy is the joule.
rubric.description: Gives the SI unit of energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for writing joule or J.

modelAnswer: Energy is the capacity to do work.
Its SI unit is the joule (J).

items.followUp: What is the difference between kinetic energy and potential energy?

rubric.why: Kinetic energy is one form of mechanical energy.
rubric.description: Identifies kinetic energy as a component of mechanical energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming kinetic energy or describing it as energy of motion.

rubric.why: Potential energy is the other form of mechanical energy.
rubric.description: Identifies potential energy as a component of mechanical energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming potential energy or describing it as energy due to position or configuration.

modelAnswer: Mechanical energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its motion or position.
It is the sum of the body’s kinetic energy and potential energy.

items.followUp: Write any two features of the kinetic molecular model of matter.

rubric.why: The model describes matter as being made of very small particles.
rubric.description: States that matter consists of tiny particles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying particles, atoms or molecules as the constituents of matter.

rubric.why: The particles of matter are in continuous motion.
rubric.description: States that particles are continuously moving.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the particles as moving continuously or randomly.

modelAnswer: Matter is made up of tiny particles.
These particles are in continuous random motion.

items.followUp: Write any two properties of gases.

rubric.why: A liquid has a definite volume.
rubric.description: States that a liquid has a definite volume.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving this property.

accept: takes the shape of its container
rubric.why: A liquid has no definite shape and can flow; it is also slightly compressible.
rubric.description: Gives another correct property of a liquid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one valid property apart from definite volume.

modelAnswer: A liquid has a definite volume.
It has no definite shape and takes the shape of its container.
